title: A seed takes its time
question: How does a small bean become a growing plant?
idea: Water helps a bean begin. A root reaches down, a shoot reaches up, and leaves open to the light.

math.title: A little taller, day by day
math.intro: These are made-up measurements of one bean plant. Real plants grow at different speeds. Measure height from the soil to the top of the plant.
math.parentNote: 3 min: read the table. 9 min: solve with drawings or number jumps. 3 min: explain. cm means centimeters. These are pretend data, not a growth promise. No real plant or ruler is needed.

plate.alt: A young bean in a pot beside a ruler, a blank notebook, and a pencil.
plate.caption: Look closely. Keep a little record.

tasks: From Day 4 to Day 8, how much taller did the plant get? Show your thinking.
On Day 12 it is 23 cm tall. Pretend it grows 9 cm more. How tall would it be?
How many days pass from Day 4 to Day 12? Count the spaces between days.
hints: Count up from 8 to 10, then from 10 to 14. How big are the two jumps together?
Split 9 into 7 and 2. Add 7 to 23 to reach 30, then add the 2 left over.
math.extension: Does the table show the same amount of growth in each four-day stretch? Explain.

reading.title: A seed takes its time
reading.parentNote: 3 min: wonder over the cover. 7 min: read and revisit the six changes. 5 min: talk about the questions. Accept pointing and oral answers. Pictures show stages, not a fixed timetable.

beats.title: A seed takes its time
beats.passage: Come to the garden. Something small is beginning. Grown-up reads; little wonderer opens the story.

plate.alt: A young bean plant and one dry seed on a sunlit garden sill.
plate.caption: A small beginning. A whole garden of possibility.

beats.title: A small, quiet beginning
beats.label: Dry seed
beats.passage: A dry bean rests in the soil. Its seed coat protects a tiny plant and a store of food inside. It has not begun to grow.

plate.alt: An intact ivory bean seed rests in loose garden soil.
plate.caption: Dry seed · a tiny plant waits inside.

beats.title: A drink, then a change
beats.label: Soak
beats.passage: Water soaks into the bean. It swells. With water, air, and enough warmth, the tiny plant can begin to grow.

plate.alt: A swollen bean seed takes in water from damp soil.
plate.caption: Water enters · the seed swells.

beats.title: The coat opens
beats.label: Split
beats.passage: The seed coat splits. A small root tip peeks out. The bean has begun to sprout. It uses food stored in its two thick seed halves.

plate.alt: The thin seed coat splits; a tiny root tip begins to emerge.
plate.caption: Seed coat splits · growth begins.

beats.title: First, a root reaches down
beats.label: Root
beats.passage: The root grows down. It takes in water and helps hold the young plant in place. The bean does not need to eat dirt.

plate.alt: A white root grows down from a bean seed into the soil.
plate.caption: Root first · down into the soil.

beats.title: Then, a shoot reaches up
beats.label: Shoot
beats.passage: A curved shoot pushes up through the soil. It lifts the thick seed halves. Below, the root keeps growing. This happens over days, not one quick moment.

plate.alt: A hooked bean shoot lifts the seed halves above the soil; roots remain below.
plate.caption: Shoot next · up toward the light.

beats.title: Open to the light
beats.label: Leaves
beats.passage: Green leaves open above the seed halves. With light, water, and air, the leaves make food for the plant. A small bean has become a seedling.

plate.alt: Two green leaves open above the smaller, thick seed halves; roots spread below.
plate.caption: True leaves open above the plump seed halves.

beats.title: Which part comes first?
beats.passage: Which grows out first: the root or the shoot? Find words in the story that helped you.

plate.alt: A white root grows down from a bean seed into the soil.
plate.caption: Root first · down into the soil.

beats.title: Food for a beginning
beats.passage: Where does the bean get food before its green leaves open?

plate.alt: The thin seed coat splits; a tiny root tip begins to emerge.
plate.caption: Seed coat splits · growth begins.

beats.title: Does a plant eat dirt?
beats.passage: A friend says, “The bean eats dirt to grow.” Help your friend look again.
choices: Yes. Roots eat pieces of dirt.
No. First it uses food stored in the seed.
feedback: The root takes in water. The seed has stored food. Try again, or look back together.
You noticed the stored food. Later, green leaves make food with light, water, and air. Soil also supplies minerals.

plate.alt: Two green leaves open above the smaller, thick seed halves; roots spread below.
plate.caption: True leaves open above the plump seed halves.

beats.title: Small changes. New life.
beats.passage: You followed a seed into the light. Tell someone one change you noticed, or carry the story onto your page.

plate.alt: A young bean plant and one dry seed on a sunlit garden sill.
plate.caption: A small beginning. A whole garden of possibility.

words.meaning: the outside covering that protects a seed
begin to grow from a seed
the part that takes in water and helps hold a plant in place

writing.title: Teach a friend how it grows
writing.intro: Your friend has never watched a bean grow. Help them picture the changes.

plate.alt: A young bean in a pot beside a ruler, a blank notebook, and a pencil.
plate.caption: Look closely. Keep a little record.

writing.parentNote: 3 min: say the steps. 4 min: draw. 6 min: write three short sentences. 2 min: reread. Accept invented spelling, pointing, or dictation. Look for water, root, then shoot and leaves.
writing.draw: Draw three moments: a bean taking in water, a root reaching down, and a shoot with leaves. Label seed, root, and leaf.

frames.hint: What comes out and grows down?

writing.check: Read your steps aloud. Could your friend follow them? Check a capital and an end mark in each sentence.

answers.label: Math · 1
answers.text: 6 cm taller. Count up: 8 + 2 = 10; 10 + 4 = 14. The jumps total 6. Check: 8 + 6 = 14.

answers.label: Math · 2
answers.text: 32 cm. Split 9 into 7 + 2: 23 + 7 = 30, then 30 + 2 = 32. This is a pretend extension, not a prediction.

answers.label: Math · 3
answers.text: 8 days pass: 12 - 4 = 8. There are nine day labels but eight spaces between them. Extension: no. The two four-day stretches show 6 cm and 9 cm of growth.

answers.label: Reading · 1
answers.text: The root comes first. Evidence: “A small root tip peeks out.” Later: “A curved shoot pushes up through the soil.”

answers.label: Reading · 2
answers.text: Food is stored in the two thick seed halves (cotyledons). Digital check: choose the stored-food answer. Roots absorb water and minerals; leaves later make food using light, water, and carbon dioxide from air.

answers.label: Writing
answers.text: Example: “First, water soaks into the bean. Next, a root grows down. Then, a shoot grows up and leaves open.” Look for three moments and seed, root, and leaf labels. Spoken explanations count.

parentGuidance: This day shows a common garden bean. Seed halves store food; true leaves unfold above them. Germination needs water, oxygen, and a suitable temperature. Later the plant needs light to keep growing. The stages overlap; timing and height vary. The pictures are enlarged illustrations, not measurements. Use the pictures today; a real growing experiment is optional. Pause between sessions.
